question: What relative lengths are shown in Figure 6B-2 for a merging taper, shifting taper, and shoulder taper?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 6B-2 shows the merging taper with a length of L, the shifting taper with a length of ½ L, and the shoulder taper with a length of ⅓ L. These relative lengths reflect the text of Section 6B.08, which describes a merging taper of at least L, a shifting taper of approximately ½ L, and a shoulder taper of approximately ⅓ L. Guidance (recommended): - "A shifting taper should have a length of approximately ½ L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4)." - "If used, shoulder tapers should have a length of approximately ¹⁄3 L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4). If a shoulder is used as a travel lane, either through practice or during a TTC activity, a normal merging or shifting taper should be used." - "The appropriate taper length (L) should be determined using the criteria shown in Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4." Support (informational): - "Tapers are created by using a series of channelizing devices and/or pavement markings to move traffic out of or into the normal path. Types of tapers are shown in Figure 6B-2. … Merging Taper at least L; Shifting Taper at least 0.5 L." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 6B-2 labels the merging taper with dimension "L," the shifting tapers with "1/2 L," and the shoulder taper with "1/3 L," along with a "4S ft*" dimension for the one-lane, two-way taper and a footnote that S = speed in mph. [Image 2] The full-page view of Figure 6B-2 (Types of Tapers and Buffer Spaces) confirms the same relative lengths: L for the merging taper, ½ L for shifting tapers, and ⅓ L for the shoulder taper, with a note to see Table 6B-4 for taper length formulas. [Image 3] Page 776 contains the Section 6B.08 guidance text stating that a shifting taper should be approximately ½ L and a shoulder taper approximately ⅓ L. [Image 4] Figure 6B-3 illustrates the one-lane, two-way traffic taper (50 to 100 ft) and downstream taper, complementing the taper types shown in Figure 6B-2. [Image 5] Figure 6P-38 (TA-38) shows these taper lengths applied in a typical application, including a shoulder taper and dimensions such as ½ L, L, and 2L. Citations: - Section 6B.08 Support §2 (p.775) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §8 (p.776) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §10 (p.776) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §4 (p.775) - Figure 6B-2 (p.774) - Page 815 - Page 817 - Page 818 - Page 976
gold_answer: Merging taper: L; shifting taper: 1/2 L; shoulder taper: 1/3 L.
